neuromuscular-junction.short: The junction where a motor neuron's ending meets a muscle fibre across a tiny gap, and passes the signal on by releasing acetylcholine.

acetylcholine.short: A chemical messenger released by nerve endings. It excites skeletal muscle at the neuromuscular junction and, released by the nerves to the heart, slows it.

acetylcholinesterase.short: The enzyme in the gap at the neuromuscular junction that breaks acetylcholine down within milliseconds, ending each signal.

safety-factor.short: Transmitter released per nerve impulse divided by the amount needed to trigger a muscle action potential. About 3–5 in healthy adult mammals.

ec-coupling.short: The chain from a muscle action potential to contraction: the signal runs into the fibre down tiny tubes (T-tubules), the sarcoplasmic reticulum releases calcium, and calcium binding to troponin lets the cross-bridges pull.

motor-unit.short: One motor neuron plus all the muscle fibres it supplies. When the neuron fires, all its fibres contract.

size-principle.short: Motor units are recruited in order of motor neuron size: small, slow, fatigue-resistant units first, large, fast, forceful units last.

rate-coding.short: Grading muscle force by changing how often motor units fire action potentials, as opposed to how many units are recruited.

mvc.short: The most force a person can produce on purpose. Forces are often given as % MVC.

sympathetic.short: The branch of the autonomic nervous system that prepares the body for effort and stress: among other things it speeds the heart and makes each beat stronger.

parasympathetic.short: The branch of the autonomic nervous system for rest and digestion. Through the vagus nerve and acetylcholine it slows the heart.

vagal-tone.short: The steady braking of heart rate by the vagus nerve at rest. It keeps resting HR well below the heart's own pacemaker rate.

sa-node-pacemaker.short: The heart's own pacemaker in the right atrium. Left alone it fires about 100 times a minute; autonomic nerves speed or slow it.

rr-interval.short: The time between two heartbeats, from one beat's main spike (the R peak) on an ECG, the heart's electrical trace, to the next, in ms. HR (beats·min⁻¹) = 60,000 ÷ RR.

hrv.short: The beat-to-beat variation in RR intervals. Short-term HRV mostly reflects vagal (parasympathetic) activity.

rmssd.short: Root mean square of successive RR differences: square each beat-to-beat difference, average them, take the square root. The main measure of the vagal part of HRV.

motor-neuron.short: A nerve cell in the spinal cord whose long fibre (the axon) runs out to a muscle and tells its muscle fibres when to contract.

autonomic-nervous-system.short: The part of the nervous system that runs the body's automatic jobs, such as heart rate, blood vessel width, sweating and digestion, without conscious control. Its two branches are sympathetic and parasympathetic.

vagus-nerve.short: The main parasympathetic nerve, running from the brainstem to the heart, lungs and gut. At the heart it releases acetylcholine and slows the beat.
